focus: Tier one is closed. Now on tier two: four parcels running, starting with the sound-driver lockup and the checks that only exist for one asset.

inFlight.what: LS-11: a music-start wait spins forever if an interrupt lands in it, and the watchdog counts the wrong loop. Only reachable in the profile that can play music, so a green canonical build proves nothing here.
LS-9: the check binding an asset's two frame tables exists for exactly one asset out of eight. Making it apply to all of them may turn an existing disagreement red, which would be the point.
LS-10: eight object slots that are never used in a release build are swept three times a frame. Skipping them rests entirely on that never-used claim, which is being re-derived by a different route.
LS-14: retire a style checker whose subject shrank to eight lines while 412 tests kept maintaining it. The job is mostly proving what retiring it loses.

blockedOnOwner.what: Whether a shipped game should spend a little ROM so a corrupt compressed stream crashes legibly instead of running off into memory. Taste, not correctness.
Whether you can actually hear a 60 Hz artefact on the drums. If you can, the controller read gets split so no pause exceeds one sample; if not, only the comments get fixed.

nextBoundary: After this tier-2 wave lands. LS-12 goes out the moment LS-11 clears the sound driver.
